newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse bouyed by financials.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse bouyed by financials.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) was buoyant on Friday, driven by strong demand for financials, brokers and bourse officials said.
The NSE 20-share index went up 36.81 points to 3234.88. Turnover was posted at 30.354 million shillings on 798,034 shares from 30.820 million shillings traded on 391,117 shares on Wednesday.
Brokers and bourse officials said the market was very active -- with most activity focused on the financials.
Credit Finance Bank traded 247,174 shares at 19.05 from 19, while Barclays Bank traded 9,442 shares at 104 unchanged.
Brokers attributed the overall price rise to excitement about upcoming year-end results.
Kenya Commercial Bank closed at 85 from 80 while Standard Chartered Bank traded at 50 unchanged.
National carrier Kenya Airways, which appears to have turned round, edged up 20 cents to close at 9.25. Power distribution monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting jumped to 166 from 158.
"Foreigners have started buying Kenya Power which is why the price is rising steadily," a senior broker said.
Rea Vipingo traded at 10.05 unchanged while Nation Printers and Publishers eased to 110 from 111.
